title: OSHA construction welding and cutting practice questions
description: Free OSHA construction welding and cutting practice questions on 29 CFR 1926 Subpart J. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: Compressed gas cylinders on a construction site are to be hoisted to an upper floor. How does 1926.350(a)(2) require them to be secured?

options.A: With a lifting magnet
options.B: With a choker sling around the cylinder body
options.C: On a cradle, slingboard, or pallet
options.D: By a hook through the valve protection cap

questions.explanation: "When cylinders are hoisted, they shall be secured on a cradle, slingboard, or pallet." The rule adds that they "shall not be hoisted or transported by means of magnets or choker slings."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.350, Gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A cylinder is frozen to the ground. What does 1926.350(a)(5) say to use to thaw it loose?

options.A: Warm, not boiling, water
options.B: Boiling water
options.C: A bar placed under the valve protection cap
options.D: The flame of a cutting torch

questions.explanation: "Warm, not boiling, water shall be used to thaw cylinders loose." The same paragraph says bars "shall not be used under valves or valve protection caps to pry cylinders loose when frozen."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.350, Gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Oxygen cylinders are stored 8 feet from fuel-gas cylinders. Under 1926.350(a)(10), which of these would be one of the allowed ways to separate them?

options.A: A canvas tarp hung between the two groups
options.B: A noncombustible barrier 3 feet high
options.C: Moving them to 12 feet apart
options.D: A noncombustible barrier at least 5 feet high with a fire-resistance rating of at least one-half hour

questions.explanation: Oxygen cylinders in storage must be separated from fuel-gas cylinders "a minimum distance of 20 feet (6.1 m) or by a noncombustible barrier at least 5 feet (1.5 m) high having a fire-resistance rating of at least one-half hour."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.350, Gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Welding must be done inside a confined space. What does 1926.350(b)(4) say about the oxygen and acetylene cylinders?

options.A: They may go in if the space is ventilated
options.B: They shall not be taken into confined spaces
options.C: They may go in if an attendant stays outside
options.D: They may go in if they are less than half full

questions.explanation: "Cylinders containing oxygen or acetylene or other fuel gas shall not be taken into confined spaces."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.350, Gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Fuel gas, manifolds, hose and torches
questions.question: For quick closing, what is the most that 1926.350(d)(2) allows a valve on a fuel gas cylinder to be opened?

options.A: Fully open
options.B: 1 1/2 turns
options.C: 3 turns
options.D: 2 1/2 turns

questions.explanation: "For quick closing, valves on fuel gas cylinders shall not be opened more than 1 1/2 turns."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.350, Gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Fuel gas, manifolds, hose and torches
questions.question: When a fuel gas cylinder valve is opened, gas is found leaking around the valve stem. What is the first step 1926.350(d)(5) requires?

options.A: Close the valve and tighten the gland nut
options.B: Keep working and check the leak at the end of the shift
options.C: Wrap the valve stem with tape
options.D: Remove the regulator with the valve still open

questions.explanation: If there is a leak around the valve stem, "the valve shall be closed and the gland nut tightened." If that does not stop the leak, "the use of the cylinder shall be discontinued, and it shall be properly tagged and removed from the work area."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.350, Gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Fuel gas, manifolds, hose and torches
questions.question: Parallel sections of oxygen and fuel gas hose are taped together. What is the most tape coverage 1926.350(f)(2) allows?

options.A: 8 inches out of 12 inches
options.B: The full length of the hose
options.C: Not more than 4 inches out of 12 inches
options.D: 6 inches out of 12 inches

questions.explanation: "When parallel sections of oxygen and fuel gas hose are taped together, not more than 4 inches out of 12 inches shall be covered by tape."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.350, Gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Fuel gas, manifolds, hose and torches
questions.question: A hose has been subject to flashback. What test does 1926.350(f)(4) set for it?

options.A: A test at its normal working pressure only
options.B: A test at 1 1/2 times its normal pressure
options.C: A test at 100 p.s.i.
options.D: A test to twice its normal pressure, but in no case less than 300 p.s.i.

questions.explanation: Hose that has been subject to flashback "shall be tested to twice the normal pressure to which it is subject, but in no case less than 300 p.s.i."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.350, Gas welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1926.351(b)(2), for what minimum distance from the end where the electrode holder is connected must welding cable generally be free from repair or splices?

options.A: 10 feet
options.B: 3 feet
options.C: 5 feet
options.D: 1 foot

questions.explanation: "Only cable free from repair or splices for a minimum distance of 10 feet from the cable end to which the electrode holder is connected shall be used," except for cables with standard insulated connectors or with splices whose insulating quality equals that of the cable.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.351, Arc welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Which of these does 1926.351(c)(2) prohibit using as a ground return?

options.A: A ground return cable rated above the unit's maximum output
options.B: A conduit containing electrical circuits
options.C: A dedicated ground return cable serving a single unit
options.D: A ground return cable serving two units and rated for their total output

questions.explanation: "Pipelines containing gases or flammable liquids, or conduits containing electrical circuits, shall not be used as a ground return."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.351, Arc welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: One ground return cable services three arc welding units. What current-carrying capacity does 1926.351(c)(1) require of it?

options.A: Equal to the output of the largest unit
options.B: Equal to the average output of the three units
options.C: Half of the total output of the three units
options.D: Equal to or exceeding the total specified maximum output capacities of all three units

questions.explanation: When a single ground return cable services more than one unit, "its safe current-carrying capacity shall equal or exceed the total specified maximum output capacities of all the units which it services."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.351, Arc welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: An arc welding machine is about to be moved to another part of the site. What does 1926.351(d)(3) require?

options.A: Lower the current setting before moving it
options.B: Cool the electrode holder in water
options.C: Open the power supply switch to the equipment
options.D: Leave the electrode in the holder and hang it on a cylinder

questions.explanation: When the welder leaves or stops work for any appreciable length of time, "or when the arc welding or cutting machine is to be moved, the power supply switch to the equipment shall be opened."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.351, Arc welding and cutting (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: When does 1926.352(e) require additional personnel to be assigned to guard against fire?

options.A: When the operation is such that normal fire prevention precautions are not sufficient
options.B: Only when the work lasts longer than four hours
options.C: Only when the work is more than 6 feet above a lower level
options.D: Only when the welder asks for a helper

questions.explanation: "When the welding, cutting, or heating operation is such that normal fire prevention precautions are not sufficient, additional personnel shall be assigned to guard against fire."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.352, Fire prevention (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: A torch and hose are used inside a confined space. What does 1926.352(g) require at the change of shifts?

options.A: Close the torch valves and leave the torch inside
options.B: Coil the hose near the opening of the space
options.C: Leave them inside if an attendant stays outside
options.D: Remove the torch and hose from the confined space

questions.explanation: "Overnight and at the change of shifts, the torch and hose shall be removed from the confined space."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.352, Fire prevention (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: What does 1926.353(a)(6) say about using oxygen to blow dust from clothing?

options.A: It is allowed at low pressure
options.B: Oxygen shall not be used for that purpose
options.C: It is allowed outdoors only
options.D: It is allowed through a regulator

questions.explanation: "Oxygen shall not be used for ventilation purposes, comfort cooling, blowing dust from clothing, or for cleaning the work area."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.353, Ventilation and protection in welding, cutting, and heating (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Sufficient ventilation for welding in a confined space cannot be obtained without blocking the means of access. What does 1926.353(b)(2) require?

options.A: Block the access while welding and reopen it afterward
options.B: Filter-type respirators, with no one needed outside
options.C: Air line respirators, with an employee outside assigned to maintain communication and aid in an emergency
options.D: Limit each welder to 15 minutes inside the space

questions.explanation: Employees in the confined space "shall be protected by air line respirators," and "an employee on the outside of such a confined space shall be assigned to maintain communication with those working within it and to aid them in an emergency."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.353, Ventilation and protection in welding, cutting, and heating (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Toxic metals and inert-gas metal-arc welding
questions.question: Welding involves beryllium-containing base metal in an enclosed space. What protection does 1926.353(c)(2)(iv) require?

options.A: General mechanical ventilation only
options.B: Either local exhaust ventilation or air line respirators
options.C: Both local exhaust ventilation and air line respirators
options.D: A filter-type respirator only

questions.explanation: "Because of its high toxicity, work involving beryllium shall be done with both local exhaust ventilation and air line respirators."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.353, Ventilation and protection in welding, cutting, and heating (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.topic: Toxic metals and inert-gas metal-arc welding
questions.question: For inert-gas metal-arc welding, what minimum distance does 1926.353(d)(1)(i) set between the use of chlorinated solvents and the exposed arc, unless shielded?

options.A: 200 feet
options.B: 25 feet
options.C: 50 feet
options.D: 100 feet

questions.explanation: "The use of chlorinated solvents shall be kept at least 200 feet, unless shielded, from the exposed arc."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.353, Ventilation and protection in welding, cutting, and heating (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: According to 1926.354(a), when are preservative coatings considered to be highly flammable?

options.A: When they are more than one coat thick
options.B: When they are less than a year old
options.C: When they are any color other than gray
options.D: When scrapings burn with extreme rapidity

questions.explanation: "Preservative coatings shall be considered to be highly flammable when scrapings burn with extreme rapidity." A competent person tests a coating whose flammability is not known before work begins.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.354, Welding, cutting, and heating in way of preservative coatings (as of Nov 4, 2026)

questions.question: Heat will be applied in an enclosed space to a surface with a toxic preservative coating, and air line respirators are not used. What minimum stripping distance from the area of heat application does 1926.354(c)(1) set?

options.A: 1 inch
options.B: 4 inches
options.C: 2 inches
options.D: 1/2 inch

questions.explanation: In enclosed spaces, surfaces with toxic preservatives "shall be stripped of all toxic coatings for a distance of at least 4 inches from the area of heat application, or the employees shall be protected by air line respirators."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1926.354, Welding, cutting, and heating in way of preservative coatings (as of Nov 4, 2026)
